title: Align account ORM relationships with declared database delete cascades
classification: Confirmed BE-009 lifecycle defects found by a populated fixture: deleting a user caused SQLAlchemy to issue NULL updates against non-nullable CASCADE foreign keys.

change.behavior: The User backrefs for these private account-owned rows now set passive_deletes='all', leaving deletion to the already declared PostgreSQL ON DELETE CASCADE constraints.
change.schema: No migration was needed; ORM relationship behavior was inconsistent with the existing schema constraints.

verification.result: passed: 12 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6.
verification.database: Fresh uniquely named PostgreSQL test database upgraded through d6e7f8a9b0c1.
verification.cleanup: The disposable test database was dropped after the passing run.
verification.coverage: The populated deletion fixture inserts a synthetic row for every one of the 50 current user-FK columns, calls the real deletion service, and checks each row against its declared disposition. Existing cases also verify file cleanup, shared chat/emoji/save preservation, credential isolation, transaction rollback, retry, and concurrent last-admin deletion.

limits: The fixtures use current ORM and Alembic schemas; deployed operator schema comparison remains open.
The child/adult/admin/shared-channel-owner/departed-download-history/external-store-disconnect tabletop and production restart/restore qualification remain open.
